title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: Line \(\ell_1\) has equation \(3x - 2y = 1\) and goes through \(A = (-1, -2).\) Line \(\ell_2\) has equation \(y = 1\) and meets line \(\ell_1\) at point \(B.\) Line \(\ell_3\) has positive slope, goes through point \(A,\) and meets \(\ell_2\) at point \(C.\) The area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(3.\) What is the slope of \(\ell_3?\)

solutions.text: Solving \(3x - 2y = 1\) with \(y = 1\) gives \(B = (1, 1).\) The distance from \(A = (-1, -2)\) to the line \(y = 1\) is \(3,\) so \(\tfrac12\cdot BC\cdot 3 = 3\) gives \(BC = 2.\) Then \(C = (3, 1)\) or \(C = (-1, 1);\) the latter makes \(\ell_3\) vertical, so \(C = (3, 1)\) and the slope is \(\dfrac{1 - (-2)}{3 - (-1)} = \dfrac34.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The distance from \(A\) to line \(\ell_2\) is \(3,\) so \(\tfrac12\cdot BC\cdot 3 = 3\) gives \(BC\)
